title: plugin-calendar: `object-calendar-renderer.propsContract.test.tsx` escapes to the real network on 127.0.0.1:3000 (4 ECONNREFUSED, same class as #3339 / #5225 / #5280)
body:
Found while working #5421 — this is the stderr noise that the coverage-lane logs show and that a reader could mistake for the shard failure. It is **not** a failure: the run stays green. Filed unassigned.

## Measured

From the repo root of a clean worktree on `main` (`9f7d786bd`), the file standing alone:

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-calendar/src/object-calendar-renderer.propsContract.test.tsx
```

emits exactly four of these and then passes:

```
Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000
    at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (node:net:1637:16) {
  errno: -111,
  code: 'ECONNREFUSED',
  syscall: 'connect',
  address: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 3000
}
```

Attribution was confirmed twice: a single-worker sequential run of a 27-file subset (`--maxWorkers=1 --fileParallelism=false`) prints the four errors in the middle of this file's own case list, between the `locale`-rejection cases and the `onEventClick` cases; and the file alone reproduces all four.

Coverage is irrelevant to it — the same four appear with and without `--coverage`, so the green PR lane carries this noise today as well. On CI the same four appear as `AggregateError` with both `::1:3000` and `127.0.0.1:3000` legs, because the runner has IPv6.

## Mechanism

`happy-dom`'s default document origin is `http://localhost:3000/`, so any relative-URL `fetch` that nothing intercepts resolves against that origin and leaves the process for real. No test file in the shard stubs `fetch` for this path — the request comes from the component graph under test, on the branch where the node does **not** carry the declared `data` pre-fetch array and the component therefore runs its own fetch.

Same defect class as #3339 (plugin-detail), #5225 (plugin-report) and #5280 (plugin-dashboard `DatasetWidget`), all closed. This is a new member of it, not a regression of those.

## Why it is worth closing

- It is a real, unhandled outbound connection from a unit test: on any machine where something *is* listening on port 3000, the assertion outcome depends on what that server answers.
- It makes every coverage-lane log carry four scary-looking network stack traces that have nothing to do with the run's verdict — which is precisely how #5421 came to be filed against the wrong mechanism.

Fix shape follows the closed siblings: give the component's own fetch path a stub (or author the `data` pre-fetch array on the nodes that do not need to exercise the fetching branch), so nothing in the file reaches the network.
